newsitem.title: PERU: Nobel winner criticizes Peru's human rights record.
newsitem.headline: Nobel winner criticizes Peru's human rights record.

text.p: Nobel Peace Laureate Jose Ramos Horta on Monday said Peruvians lived under a dictatorship and criticised the government's human rights record.
"The majority of public opinion in your country believes that there is a dictatorship, and I cannot disagree with what Peruvians think," he told reporters at Peru's Congress.
President Alberto Fujimori has come under increasing fire in recent weeks, and plunged in opinion polls to his lowest level, on perceptions of his authoritarianism.

He has been widely criticised for his government's moves against Peru's highest constitutional court and the media, cases of torture in the intelligence service, and political manoeuvres towards a possible re-election bid in 2000.
"I am amazed and I believe that the government should respect the independence of various institutions, like the tribunals, the judiciary and the press," Ramos told reporters.
"Torturing is cowardly, condemnable from all points of view and should be banned from the face of this earth," he added.
Ramos, a campaigner for self-determination for East Timor, won the Nobel peace prize in 1996 and is touring South America to promote independence for his country.
